event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: A meticulous review of the 2024-02-28 NRG Form 10-K text provided reveals no explicit reference to COVID-19, ‘coronavirus,’ ‘pandemic,’ ‘epidemic,’ or any synonymous language describing pandemic-related impacts such as supply-chain interruptions, remote-work transitions, labour shortages, or demand shocks. The risk discussion is extensive—covering commodity volatility, weather, cyber-security, regulatory change, and many other contingencies—but global-health events are conspicuously absent. Given the filing date, the COVID-19 outbreak sits just under four years in the past, placing it in the early part of the Time-Decay “medium-term” band (4–10 years, expected scores 4-6). If any pandemic-specific disclosure existed, it would likely draw a moderate score. However, because the document does not acknowledge the pandemic at all, there is no evidentiary basis for assigning any score above zero. The absence itself signals that management no longer views COVID-19 as a material standalone risk, or that any residual effects are subsumed under more generic categories (e.g., “catastrophic events,” “supply disruption”). Consequently, no qualifying sentences can be extracted, and the overall risk indicator for this event within this filing is effectively null.
